newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares inch higher, boosted by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares inch higher, boosted by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed 0.13 percent higher on Wednesday, boosted by strong gains in drug maker Lek, but traders said most market activity was dominated by book-balancing ahead of the end of the month.
"Everybody is waiting for prices to be boosted when foreigners return to buying," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska bank.
The key SBI index rose 1.69 points to 1,316.56. Turnover rose to 30.9 million tolars from 19.4 million. Overall 10 shares rose, four fell and 13 were untraded.
"Traders eagerly await fresh foreign capital to help revive market activity," Jarc added.

The blue-chip SBI was knocked down more then 20 percent after the central bank in February blocked international investment by requiring foreign investors to open custodian accounts with local banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian shares.
Banks expect the first such accounts to be opened in May.
Issue A of drug firm Lek was among the day's biggest winners, rising 2.11 percent to 24,710 tolars on volume of 221 shares.
"Lek will remain one of the most interesting shares on the market," one trader said.
The top gainer was mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska, jumping 7.9 percent to 1,749 tolars on volume of 2,069 shares.
Traders traced the advance to a technical correction to a more than 12 percent decline in Radenska's shares over the past three trading sessions.
Aroma maker Etol had the highest turnover, firming 0.06 percent to 17,510 tolars on volume of 600 shares for total turnover of 10.5 million.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, falling 6.67 percent to 7,000 shares on volume of seven shares.
The Ljubljana bourse will be closed on Thursday and Friday.
